ledger.hypothesis: compute() does no arithmetic worth measuring (one double compare, three float stores). Every microsecond is API and DG overhead, so the only lever is call count. Three calls were pure waste: MDataHandle::asString() on audioFile returns an MString BY VALUE (refcount + heap copy) and the result was immediately discarded via (void)in_aAudioFile; a `static std::vector<NodeState*>` was linearly scanned on (const void*)this every eval to find a single bool; and the codegen prologue did set3Float(0,0,0) that every branch below overwrote. Removing all three should cut the controllable slice roughly in half.
ledger.risk: Eliding the audioFile datablock read is the only change with a semantic edge. It is safe because `color` has zero numerical dependence on audioFile (the whole audio block is ND_PORT_INCOMPLETE -- it needs disk I/O and QMediaPlayer, neither of which exists in a compiled compute), and because the attributeAffects(aAudioFile, aColor*) wiring is left completely intact, so the plug contract and dirty propagation are unchanged. Second risk: asDouble() in place of asAngle().asRadians() could have silently returned 0.0 on a kAngle handle, which would have made every eval red and failed parity -- so it was not assumed, it was VERIFIED in-situ with a one-shot print on a warmup call (asDouble=3.49066e-05, asRadians=3.49066e-05, `==` true) before being adopted. The threshold compare keeps the source's type (double), direction (<) and strictness, so the tie at 0.165009870842 resolves identically.
ledger.theme: This node is neither elementwise nor query-shaped -- it is a two-branch scalar compare whose entire cost is per-call Maya API overhead, so the win is deleting the API calls that produce nothing: the unused audioFile MString read, the static-registry scan over `this`, and a dead zero-write to the colour output.

ledger.hypothesis: The node is neither ELEMENTWISE nor QUERY shaped: its only inputs are a scalar angle and an unused string, and its only output is a 3-float colour. There is no N and no M, so no acceleration structure, no parallel map and no cross-evaluation cache can apply (the one input that matters, angle, is perturbed by the harness on every tick by design, so any cache would be a guaranteed miss and any output memo would be a parity failure). I predicted before measuring that nothing would move the number, and that the honest deliverable was a leaner-but-identical compute plus the evidence for why the floor is where it is.
ledger.risk: The latch reduction is the only place correctness could slip. In the Python, the red path reads `if not self.pain: self.pain = True` -- the guard exists ONLY to fire the one-shot playback, which is unported, so the assignment is unconditional in effect and the path always ENDS with pain==true; the green path always sets it false. `_pain = painful` is therefore exactly equivalent, not merely close. The threshold test keeps the source's type (double), direction and strictness (`<`), so an exact tie at 0.165009870842 resolves to the same branch it did before; blue is 0.0f on both paths, and the ternaries select between exact constants, so no arithmetic was introduced that could round differently.
ledger.theme: This node has no array, geometry or query work at all -- compute() is one scalar read, one compare and a 3-float write -- so the only change worth making was collapsing the two set3Float call sites into one; the node was already at the harness's measurement floor.
